newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Hindalco sees lower 96/97 net. [CORRECTED 6:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: India's Hindalco sees lower 96/97 net. [CORRECTED 6:45 GMT]

text.p: India's largest private aluminium maker Hindalco Industries said on Wednesday its net profit will see a "marginal decline" in 1996/97 (April-March) from 4.01 billion rupees a year earlier.

"The decline is on account of power disturbance caused by a grid failure in April 1996 which resulted in a production loss of about 7,000 metric (Corrects from "million" to "metric") tonnes (MT)," Hindalco said in a written response to a questionnaire by Reuters.
Hindalco said as a result of the power problems, aluminium output during 1996/97 would decline to around 167,000 MT against 175,398 MT in 1995/96.
It said alumina output was also expected to fall below the previous year.
"We anticipate alumina production to be close to 330,000 MT in 1996/97 as compared to 341,000 MT in the previous year," the firm said.
"Other factors such as the planned shutdown of our rolling mill for the purpose of modernisation, and low international prices of aluminium also had an impact on net profit," Hindalco said.
The company said exports during 1996/97 would be in excess of 26,000 MT totalling around 1.6 billion rupees.
"This represents an increase of approximately 52 percent in terms of value and 62 percent in terms of quantity over the previous year," Hindalco said.
